title: Understanding the Bias-Variance Decomposition
text: The bias-variance decomposition is a way to express the expected error of a model as the sum of three components: bias, variance, and irreducible error. In this context, we are interested in understanding what $E[Y-f_{\hat{\theta}}(x)]$ represents.

title: What is Model Bias?
text: Model bias refers to the error introduced by approximating a real-world problem, which may be complex, by a simplified model. It is the difference between the expected prediction of our model and the true value we are trying to predict.

title: Relating Bias to the Expression
text: In the bias-variance decomposition, the term $E[Y-f_{\hat{\theta}}(x)]$ is related to the bias of the model. Consider how the expected prediction of the model compares to the true value.
